title: ⚖️ Eryndor Living Atlas IV — Economy, Livelihoods & Autonomous Simulation
rawNotionMarkup: Living economy simulation rules for Eryndor, Year 3,847. This is a new operating model, not retrospective rewriting of Gloin's past purchases or known politics. The world's prices, wages, harvests, armies, credit, crime, transport and food supply change from causes and decisions. The current campaign time remains Autumn Day 22, 11:25 AM, Year 3,847, until the player next acts. ## Sixfold world census is now the current baseline — 21 November 2026 Population resimulation completed: The creator explicitly accepted a 6× revision of previously simulated Year 3847 populations. The current modeled world total is 2,062.800 million residents (formerly 343.800m), with Avarra 1,019.760m, Tharvorn 171.000m, Sahrad 282.222m, Orundel 393.600m and Vaelora 196.218m. The 28-people by five-continent matrix, 133 previously quantified named settlement/Throne entries, the 18 resident categories of Bramblebridge, and the 8 other quantified patchwork places, plus habitat and carrying-capacity constraints, are audited in Eryndor Living Census XII — Sixfold Population & Carrying-Capacity Audit. Priority and supersession: All old 343.8m, 24m Khazari, 22m Seven Thrones, 18m Eldar, 31m Urakai and 3.8m Karak-Varn figures in the preserved legacy text are superseded as current demographic estimates by 6× figures. They remain intact only as historical reference or original simulation baselines. New: 144m global Khazari; 132m Seven-Throne domain subtotal included in the 144m; 22.8m Karak-Varn included in the Thrones. Do NOT add these overlapping totals. Long-lived peoples retain unchanged birth rates, and any specific community may still face housing, food, water and supply crises because the new populations are not equally concentrated. This is a historical-scale editorial resimulation, not 6× births during the current play session. No old ancient First Throne uncertain peak estimate or unnamed uncensused species is automatically multiplied. Gloin's Year 3847, Era of Crowns, Fifth Age campaign remains paused at Hadrik's desk, Autumn Day 22 \~11:25 AM. ## Rule-of-cool scope for economic research Historical examples can enrich food markets, workshops, contracts, guilds, courts, merchants, freight, labor and public services; they do not reduce established populations or disallow imaginative technological scale. Ridiculousness has no automatic impact on whether a thing works. An eccentric machine, strange trading invention or seemingly impossible project may function, or fail, based on actual in-world conditions; neither visual silliness nor impressive appearance settles the result. The owner rejects both “if it's cool enough it must succeed” and “it's ridiculous so it cannot work.” Existing economic models below are helpful worldbuilding scaffolding rather than physical ceilings, and may be adapted when a creator-approved fantasy mechanism supports an unusual city or device. The financial, logistical and political consequences of in-world events still apply. Preserve Karak-Varn at 3.8 million and all recorded balances. ## Economic ground rules from existing canon - Coins: 100 copper = 1 silver; 100 silver = 1 gold; 100 gold = 1 platinum. Other mints can have local acceptance differences without discarding common book-value accounting. - Karak-Varn baseline: common-room bed 2c; private basic room 5c; comfortable room 8c; quality inn 1s; bath/hot water 2c; breakfast 2–3c or hearty 5c; hearty meal 4–6c; ale 2c; autumn honey brew 3c. Other towns vary for transport, scarcity, risk and status. - Gloin's last verified purse 10 silver crowns and 82 copper; no deductions without an actual chosen purchase or explicit cost established in play. His Day 20 18s93c and later Day 21 spending require prior copper discrepancy audit; do not invent transactions. - Magic and technology cost training, specialized labor, supplies, maintenance and safe infrastructure. Gyrocopters, magitech war machines, airships and dragon passage are not cheap mass-market travel. - Nature of the world: kings, markets, workers, clans, sailors and predators do not exist only when Gloin visits them. Disturbances must have social and economic consequences. ## Fantasy-scale demographics and consequences of mass upheaval — creator priority Explicit creator clarification: Eryndor's population and settlement scales should be larger and more ambitious than ordinary historical comparisons. The world contains long-established civilizations, immense cities, powerful armies, terrifying monsters, advanced and wondrous technologies, and magical phenomena. Great population centers make it possible for war, invasion, disease, siege, mass enslavement, ecological disasters and magical catastrophes to cause enormous losses of life, potentially reaching hundreds of thousands or more in an extreme regional or continental crisis. These possibilities are stakes, not preset body counts. Birth-rate freeze — explicit creator instruction: Do not alter, increase, accelerate or invent birth/fertility rates to justify large populations or to replace catastrophic losses. Preserve every already established species- and region-specific reproduction pattern. Where no numerical birth rate was previously set, leave it unquantified rather than guessing one. Long historical timescales, immigration, existing settlement patterns and fantasy-world scale can coexist with unchanged births; any post-catastrophe recovery takes real in-world time and may never fully occur. Larger possible casualty totals do not imply faster births. - Don't shrink existing numbers: The accepted population of Karak-Varn remains 3.8 million, with the established Khazari, Eldar and Urakai totals untouched. The new 343.8m atlas-wide numerical model is a provisional simulation baseline, not a cap on what fantasy-scale Eryndor may contain. Other populations can be revised or expanded at the owner's direction and as new regions are developed; do not invent a population revision now merely to support a hypothetical casualty. - Large losses have persistent aftermath: Count soldiers and civilians separately where possible. Missing people, prisoners, refugees, destroyed households, abandoned hamlets, orphaned children, injured survivors, displaced artisans, food shortages, changing tax bases and intergenerational resentment can reshape a realm. Historical institutions provide inspiration for recovery, relief, rebuilding, conscription and labor migration, but cannot prohibit extraordinary fantasy events. - Not every battle kills millions: An army may retreat, a siege may lift, a catastrophe may be prevented, an epidemic may be contained. Losses and outcomes depend on the actual scale, exposure, threats, preparation, decisions, magic and defenses. Avoid exaggerating ordinary skirmishes or making devastation inevitable just to prove Eryndor is grimdark. - Demographics change over time: If destruction actually occurs during play, update the affected region's residents, refugee flows, farming labor, reconstruction, military strength, inheritance and diplomacy. A civilization can have existed for millennia while enduring expansions, disasters, migrations and recovery rather than continuous unbroken growth. - Campaign safeguard: These are possible future consequences, not a claim that an unseen mass-casualty event has already happened. The world does not advance during the current Day 22 11:25 AM pause, and Gloin knows only what he could learn in-world. ## Planetwide production model (simulated, not a revealed official census) Of the roughly 343.8m modeled residents, use a working distribution of approximately 72% in farms, woodlands, camps, herding, fisheries and small settlements; 19% in towns and regional cities; 9% in major capitals and metro infrastructure. The labels concern functional settlement patterns, not exclusively people who farm; a town also has apprentices, soldiers, clerks, brewers and dependents. A modern historian cannot literally audit every household of Eryndor. The numeric model provides consistency; game narration provides local variation. | Continent | Dominant bulk outputs | Scarce or strategic imports | Key system constraint | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Avarra | Iron, steel, weaponry, grain from Aldermere, Eldar medicines, cattle and merchant finance | Some tropical spices, hardwood, southern dyes, sea salt, specialist materials | Deepway bottlenecks, overland wars, food demand of Khazari metros | | Tharvorn | Timber, salt fish, furs, peat, wool, bog iron, hardy livestock | Winter grain, precision machine parts, tropical medicine | Winter closures, short growing season, storm shipping | | Sahrad | Dates, cotton, glass, spices, dyes, salt, river grain, metal ores in highlands | Timber, machine parts, certain cool-climate fodder, specialized steels | Irrigation, canal headwaters, drought and overland water rights | | Orundel | River grain, rice, livestock, timber, mineral ore, workshops, medicinal plants | Fine specialty tools, selected luxury goods, river engineering imports | Floodplains, enormous river traffic, pasture boundaries, jungle extraction | | Vaelora | Timber, fine woodcraft, fish, lake grain, medicinal herbs, wool, mountain ore | Imported steel, salt in upland interiors, specialty glass and dyes | Forest treaties, lake depth/portage, storm coasts | Sample regional specialisation: Sahradi glass moves by merchant ship to the Shattered Coast; Avarran steel moves to Orundel's highland forges; Tharvorn salted fish feeds Avarran border forces during poor harvests; Vaeloran herbs supply Letharion and southern apothecaries. None is an economic monopoly or an always-profitable route. ## A food-supply reality check: Karak-Varn's 3.8 million To make the huge established underground population credible, use a planning-equivalent food budget, not a magical handwave. - 3.8m people × 240 kg dry grain-calorie equivalent/year ≈ 912,000 tonnes/year. This is a rough caloric accounting unit and does not mean every person eats exclusively grain. Proteins, fungi, fish, tubers, vegetables, oils and preserved foods substitute for part of that energy. - \~65% modeled domestic equivalent: mountain terraces and outer farms, subterranean cultivated caverns, lake fish, heat/soil-managed deep food systems and allocated shared produce; depends on ordinary water, labor, nutrients, lighting or daylight shafts, engineering and repairs. - \~35% modeled external equivalent: about 319,000 tonnes/year, or roughly 885 tonnes/day on a 360-day year. At \~3 tonnes useful cargo per heavy freight wagon, that is nearly 300 loaded wagon equivalents per day on average, spread across multiple main Deepways and surface gates. This is a modeled freight-scale planning requirement, not proof a single gate handles all food. - The city therefore needs major reservoirs, food reserves, granaries, thermal regulation, sewage removal, cargo channels and a large agricultural region; its wealth is not the same as food independence. - If one major road closes for 20 days, use grain inventories, alternate rail-cart transfer sections, price escalation and rationing decisions. Don't fabricate famine within hours or keep prices perfectly unchanged for months. - The Seven Thrones each sustain their own outer agricultural contracts and underground stores; dependence differs. A surface village can be strategically important because it protects a thousand tonnes of grain more than because it contains a mysterious artifact. ## Food, infrastructure and settlement capacity - Food: Track staple grain equivalent and local specific produce; water safety, soil fertility, pasture, fishing seasons, stored reserves and transport. A famine begins with measurable failure of harvest, distribution or access, not a dramatic rumor alone. - Fuel: Wood, charcoal, coal, peat, geothermal sources and specific magitech operate at different scales. Fuel shortages can stop mine pumping, foundries, heating, glassworks, salt boiling and food preservation. - Buildings: Towns need repair crews, roofs, sewers, fire lanes, wells, granaries and shelter. A border siege often drains infrastructure labor. - Hospitals and healers: Infection, injuries, childbirth, cold, occupational exposure, animal disease and epidemics matter. Everyday spells are limited and costly; no magical healthcare eliminates ordinary medicine. - Livelihoods: Farmers, herders, fishers, miners, carters, sailors, millers, brewers, scribes, teachers, engineers, smiths, guild clerks, mercenaries and household laborers support one another. Do not assume everyone is an adventurer. - Population pressure: Long-lived peoples can be wealthy without high births. Migrant workers need lodging and legal status. War or disease changes labor availability and settlement viability. ## Initial, nonbinding wage and service quotes The following new indicative price bands complement rather than overwrite the Karak-Varn meal and lodging baselines. A character may ask for a quote, negotiate or decline. These are not existing contracts or money removed from anyone's purse. | Work or service | Suggested daily quote / unit (near Karak-Varn) | Why it varies | | --- | --- | --- | | Field/warehouse labor | 10–20 copper / day | Season, heavy loads, accommodation, food included | | Trained mason, millwright, quarry worker | 25–65 copper / day | Tools, depth, liability, guild membership | | Armored hired guard | 35–80 copper / day | Combat risks, equipment, food, insurance and reputation | | Local rural guide | 20–45 copper / day | Safe road, known territory, seasonal passage | | Deepways expert guide | 50–120 copper / day | Permits, technical skill, map knowledge and risk | | Scribe/translator | 20–90 copper / day | Script rarity, confidentiality and available records | | Experienced healer/Runecraft specialist | 1–5 silver or project fee | Degree of magic, material supplies, difficulty, risk | | Stable/pack animal feed | 3–9 copper / day | Animal size, fodder supply and winter scarcity | | Common cart space | 2–8 copper / person-day, seat only | Route, weather, tolls, baggage extra | | Guarded coach | 8–30 copper / person-day | Comfort, safety, route permits, full passenger manifest | | Sea passage, deck | 1–4 silver per port-to-port leg | Season, voyage length, meals, hazards and crowding | | Small caravan escort contract | Negotiated by day and number of guards | Employer solvency, destination, duty, injury arrangements | Critical: Gloin may be able to walk out with his axe, food and ordinary gear. He cannot assume 10s82c pays for a long intercontinental expedition or safely hire a whole company. Quoted wages are income only if he actually gets hired and works; hiring a coach requires player assent. ## Regional price indexes for basic goods (Karak-Varn = 100) These are scenario opening indicators, not fixed tariffs. Price for a particular food/tool changes with producer, quality and conditions. Inflation is localized. | Market | Staple food index | Lodging index | Iron/steel index | Main driver | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Karak-Varn | 100 | 100 | 100 | Industrial jobs, deep-city food demand, recent military iron pressure | | Copperspan | 92 | 78 | 110 | Grain access, bridge toll and finished-tool markups | | Lanternreach | 107 | 85 | 120 | Mixed border tolls, trade surges | | Elenvar, Letharion | 115 | 150 | 135 | Forest conservation and skilled fine craft | | Highmere, Aldermere | 75 | 105 | 142 | Broad grain belt and expensive imported iron | | Valenor, Valtoria | 90 | 120 | 155 | Military procurement | | Khurazh, eastern Urakai | 85 | 90 | 106 | Local herding and smithing | | Orrisport, Shattered Coast | 106 | 150 | 143 | Maritime duties and imports | | Hjarnfjord, Tharvorn | 140 | 105 | 153 | Winter grain and difficult shipping | | Qasr Meradin, Sahrad | 100 | 130 | 171 | River harvests; expensive steel hauling | | Veyrahn, Orundel | 83 | 115 | 118 | Large river grain market and busy workshops | | Lakeharbor, Vaelora | 91 | 115 | 144 | Local fish/grain and long metal transit | Example: Hearty 5-copper Karak-Varn equivalent might be 3–5c in a producing Aldermere village or 7–9c in a remote winter port, subject to actual menu and negotiation. Don't mathematically adjust all foods from one index or replace a published scene's price. ## Commerce network and supply routes | Trade artery | Core cargo | Mode / stakeholders | Disruption trigger | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | West Spine Deepway | Ore, grain, measured stone, runic tools | Seven-Throne freight guilds and toll offices | Flooded shaft, disputed customs, survey permit | | Eastern Caravan Road | Iron, cattle, leather, grain, wagons | Karak-Orun and independent Urakai trade families | Poor pasture, theft, border inspection | | Silverflow Timber & Food Road | Fruit, coppice wood, wheat, cloth | Letharion forests and western farmers | Logging treaty, bad harvest, bridge failure | | Aldermere–Valtoria North March | Grain, fodder, armor, draft animals | Border merchants, war offices, private wagoners | Mobilization, requisition, embargo | | Shattered Isles Sea Lane | Sea salt, spice, marine products, credit bills | Merchant republics and Merfolk treaty harbours | Piracy, storm, reef rights | | Crown Sea–Sahrad | Spices, dyes, dates, cotton, machinery | Sahradi courts, maritime insurers, Avarran docks | Canal closure, drought, naval convoy | | North Fjord Trade | Timber, fish, wool, peat, ore | Tharvorn ports and Northern Holds fleets | Sea ice, port disease, timber ban | | Orundel Great River Barges | Rice/grain, ore, textiles, craft products | River federations, city tolls, Merfolk estuary claimants | Flood, lock closure, navigation fee | | Western Ocean–Vaelora | Timber, fine herbs, lake fish, steel imports | Vaeloran lake/ocean ports and republic insurers | Long storm passage, warehouse fire | Individual ship schedules and road closures are recorded as they occur in-world, not invented as past completed events. ## Self-running simulation ledger: step size and accountability Every user action advances only the in-world time actually spent. The real-world time between chats does not elapse in Eryndor. Over the time advanced by Gloin's actions, distant people and systems act independently, but information takes time to reach him. ### Daily local turn (24-hour windows, or on actual elapsed shorter spans) 1. Clock and whereabouts: record exact day, location, weather season, routes attempted and time spent. No hours skipped without a narrated or implied activity. 2. Inventory: staple food, fuel, timber, ore, medicine and goods move from producers to markets, subtract consumption, spoilage, theft and exports. 3. Travel: caravans, ships, messengers, armies and individuals progress at actual supported speeds. Stops, losses, detours, inspections and fatigue count. 4. NPC life: officials attend duties, families farm, teachers keep classes, workers have shifts, criminals seek opportunity. No convenient omniscience. 5. News: rumor spreads with messengers, commerce and gossip. Gloin knows only reports reaching his physical social network. 6. Player ledger: do not change Gloin's purse, inventory or commitments without an observed or chosen event. ### Weekly political and trade turn Each region receives a state for Food, Fuel, Water, Security, Public Order, Transport, Treasury and Diplomacy, scored on a 0–5 pressure scale (0 ample/secure, 5 critical), but the score is GM bookkeeping only. An event must be motivated by evidence or a plausible background cause, not arbitrary drama tailored to Gloin. Representative starting pressures at Autumn Day 22 (new simulation estimates, not official intelligence): | Region | Food | Security | Trade disruption | Political strain | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Karak-Varn metro | 1 | 1 | 1 | 2 | | Valtorian North Marches | 2 | 3 | 2 | 3 | | Aldermere frontier | 1 | 2 | 2 | 3 | | Letharion | 1 | 1 | 1 | 2 | | Eastern Urakai Grasslands | 1 | 2 | 1 | 3 | | Tharvorn fjords | 2 | 2 | 2 | 1 | | Sahradi river oases | 2 | 2 | 1 | 2 | | Orundel river federation | 1 | 1 | 2 | 2 | | Vaelora forest marches | 1 | 2 | 2 | 2 | Pressure scores are not secretly predetermined outcomes. High security pressure raises patrol costs and rumors but is not proof of war. Chronic water deficits gradually damage crops and change migration incentives. ### Seasonal and annual turns - Every season (90 days): estimate harvest, stored food, spawning/fishing success, water, winter heating needs, disease, road conditions, festivals, fiscal revenues, debts and market prices. - Every year (360 days): births, mortality, migration, infrastructure damage/repairs, population settlements changing status, treaties, new guild branches, debt, dynastic births/deaths and long-duration education. - Planning demographic bands: Human and Urakai communities may grow faster in prosperous years, with differential by community; long-lived Khazari/Eldar often have slower annual turnover. Do not force a universal annual growth percentage across all species; local numbers change by cause. - Migration: shortages or war drive departures; opportunity and protection draw workers. The Avarran 170m is a base snapshot, not an immutable future quota. - Debt and treasury: a king's declared budget is distinct from an ability to pay. Army pay arrears, withheld wages, credit failure and speculation may affect loyalties. ### GM economic update formula (bookkeeping, not player-facing magic) For a staple commodity in a settlement at the end of a relevant period: Closing stock = Opening stock + production + lawful imports + purchases − consumption − lawful exports − spoilage − seizures/losses. For a region's market, compare estimated available stock against projected near-term use; shortage may drive prices and reduce access, but actual transaction prices must remain locally plausible and respond to buyer/quality/location. Do not create counterfeit precision by treating this simple sketch as a complete numerical world economy. ### Consequence examples, not pre-scripted events - If a southern pass collapses, Karak-Varn's food imports may reroute and rise in price, Copperspan carpenters may profit, and an isolated village may run out of lamp oil. - If Valtoria's mobilisation continues, iron and horse contracts may enrich traders while border farmers face fodder seizures; diplomacy or political opposition could halt it. - If a Merfolk reef is damaged, an island port can face embargoes and fishing losses even when surface dockworkers claim ignorance. - If a rural bridge is repaired, carts return, mills reopen, wage opportunities improve and thieves move to another crossing. - Nothing in these examples confirms an event has happened, connects to the First Throne or forces Gloin to participate. ## Practical merchant, guild and household simulation Each major city should have: - Grain weighers, bakers, butcher and fish sellers, innkeepers, carpenters, stonemasons, smiths, healers and apprentices. - Traders with inventories, warehouses, transport permits, debt, competitors, legal disputes, payroll and surviving relatives. - Courts, taxes, debt collectors, trade unions or guilds, patrols, public works and sanitation. - Religious institutions, charities, festivals and sceptics without declaring any god objectively real. - A market-board with jobs, rumors (sometimes false), warnings, local news and seasonal prices. Board notices are offers, not jobs accepted by Gloin. - Agricultural hinterland and water infrastructure capable of supporting recorded urban inhabitants. Every minor hamlet need only enough detail for play when visited: who governs, why households remain, their food and water, a distinct local problem, a trade relationship, and who will remember Gloin's actions. It must not become a template-generated mystery every time.
